content: 1. The Physical Principle In high-voltage electrical transmission grids, synchronous generator rotor kinematics and power balance are governed by the non-linear second-order Swing Equation : $$M \frac{d^2 \delta}{dt^2} + D \frac{d\delta}{dt} = P_{\text{mech}} - P_{\text{elec}}(\delta)$$ where: - $\delta(t)$ is the electrical rotor angle relative to a synchronously rotating reference frame ($50\text{ Hz}$ or $60\text{ Hz}$). - $\omega(t) = \frac{d\delta}{dt}$ is the angular speed deviation ($rad/s$). - $M = \frac{2H}{\omega_s}$ is the generator rotational inertia constant ($s^2/\text{rad}$). - $D$ is the natural damping coefficient (due to damper windings and governor dynamics). - $P_{\text{mech}}$ is mechanical turbine shaft power input. - $P_{\text{elec}}(\delta) = \frac{V_1 V_2}{X_{12}} \sin(\delta) = P_{\text{max}} \sin(\delta)$ is electrical transmitted power over transmission line impedance $X_{12}$. System electrical grid frequency is coupled to rotor deviation by: $$f(t) = f_0 + \frac{1}{2\pi} \frac{d\delta}{dt} = f_0 + \frac{\omega(t)}{2\pi}$$ Under sudden electrical faults (e.g., three-phase lightning strike on a transmission line), $P_{\text{elec}} \to 0$ instantaneously, causing rapid rotor acceleration governed by the remaining mechanical torque: $$\frac{d\omega}{dt} = \frac{P_{\text{mech}}}{M}$$ ⚛️ Physics Principle & Governing Constraint: Equal-Area Criterion for Transient Stability Transient grid stability requires that the accelerating area $A_1$ during the fault cannot exceed the maximum available decelerating area $A_2$ upon fault clearing: $$\int_{\delta_0}^{\delta_{cl}} (P_{\text{mech}} - P_{\text{elec}}^{fault}) \, d\delta \le \int_{\delta_{cl}}^{\delta_{max}} (P_{\text{elec}}^{post} - P_{\text{mech}}) \, d\delta$$ 2. The Physical Principle Solar radiant flux reaching Earth's surface undergoes atmospheric scattering and absorption described by the Beer-Lambert-Bouguer Law of radiative transfer: $$I_{\text{DNI}} = I_0 \cdot \varepsilon_0 \cdot \exp\left( - m_{\text{air}}(\theta_z) \cdot \tau_{\text{atm}} \right)$$ where: - $I_0 \approx 1361.2 \text{ W/m}^2$ is the extraterrestrial solar constant. - $\varepsilon_0 = 1 + 0.033 \cos\left( \frac{2\pi d_n}{365} \right)$ is the Earth orbital eccentricity correction factor on day of year $d_n$. - $\theta_z$ is the solar zenith angle, computed from site latitude $\phi$, solar declination $\delta$, and hour angle $\omega$: $$\cos \theta_z = \sin \phi \sin \delta + \cos \phi \cos \delta \cos \omega$$ $m_{\text{air}}(\theta_z)$ is the optical relative air mass, given by the Kasten-Young empirical formula: $$m_{\text{air}}(\theta_z) = \frac{1}{\cos \theta_z + 0.50572(96.07995 - \theta_z)^{-1.6364}}$$ $\tau_{\text{atm}}$ is total atmospheric optical depth, decomposed into four constituent physical extinction mechanisms: $$\tau_{\text{atm}} = \tau_{\text{Rayleigh}} + \tau_{\text{Ozone}} + \tau_{\text{WaterVapor}} + \tau_{\text{Aerosol}}$$ Global Horizontal Irradiance ($GHI$) on photovoltaic modules combines Direct Normal Irradiance ($DNI$) and Diffuse Horizontal Irradiance ($DHI$): $$GHI = I_{\text{DNI}} \cos \theta_z + DHI$$ ⚛️ Physics Principle & Governing Constraint: Physical Clear-Sky Index Boundary Limit The dimensionless clear-sky index $k_t = \frac{GHI}{GHI_{\text{clearsky}}}$ is physically bounded: $$0.0 \le k_t \le 1.25$$ Values of $k_t > 1.0$ occur transiently only during localized cloud-edge scattering ("cloud enhancement" phenomenon). 2. The Physical Principle Transient acoustic pressure wave propagation and fluid momentum dynamics in pressurized oil and gas pipelines are governed by the coupled 1D hyperbolic Water-Hammer PDEs : $$\frac{\partial H}{\partial t} + \frac{a^2}{g A} \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 0 \quad \text{(Continuity)}$$ $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + g A \frac{\partial H}{\partial x} + \frac{f Q |Q|}{2 D A} = 0 \quad \text{(Momentum)}$$ where: - $H(x, t)$ is piezometric pressure head ($m$). - $Q(x, t)$ is volumetric flow rate ($m^3/s$). - $a$ is the acoustic wave speed in the liquid-pipe system ($\approx 1000 - 1300\text{ m/s}$ for crude oil in steel pipelines): $$a = \sqrt{\frac{K/\rho}{1 + (K/E)(D/e) c_1}}$$ $g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2$ is gravitational acceleration. $A = \frac{\pi D^2}{4}$ is cross-sectional inner pipe area. $f$ is Darcy-Weisbach pipe friction factor. When an abrupt valve closure or pump trip occurs, the Joukowsky Equation governs the instantaneous maximum surge pressure rise: $$\Delta P_{\text{max}} = \rho \cdot a \cdot \Delta v$$ If an orifice leak exists at location $x_L \in [0, L]$, the sudden rupture acts as an acoustic discontinuity that emits localized expansion waves propagating bi-directionally toward both pipeline boundary pressure transducers. The time-difference-of-arrival ($\Delta t = t_2 - t_1$) directly determines leak locus: $$x_L = \frac{L + a \cdot \Delta t}{2}$$ ⚛️ Physics Principle & Governing Constraint: Acoustic Reflection & Energy Dissipation The leak orifice discharge obeys the Torricelli orifice equation: $$Q_{\text{leak}} = C_d A_{\text{leak}} \sqrt{2 g H_L}$$ This causes characteristic damping and phase distortion in subsequent reflected wave fronts. 2. The Physical Principle Supersonic inviscid flow over sharp airfoils is governed by the 2D Euler Equations of gas dynamics: $$\frac{\partial}{\partial x} \begin{bmatrix} \rho u \\ \rho u^2 + p \\ \rho u v \\ (E + p)u \end{bmatrix} + \frac{\partial}{\partial y} \begin{bmatrix} \rho v \\ \rho u v \\ \rho v^2 + p \\ (E + p)v \end{bmatrix} = 0$$ For supersonic freestream Mach numbers $M_\infty > 1$, local surface pressure behind attached oblique shock waves and Prandtl-Meyer expansion fans is governed by Shock-Expansion Theory : $$\frac{p_2}{p_1} = 1 + \frac{2\gamma}{\gamma + 1} (M_{1n}^2 - 1)$$ For thin airfoils at angle of attack $\alpha$, the Ackeret linearized supersonic pressure coefficient relation simplifies to: $$C_p = \frac{2 \theta}{\sqrt{M_\infty^2 - 1}}$$ where $\theta$ is local surface inclination angle relative to freestream vector. Lift and wave drag coefficients satisfy: $$C_L = \frac{4 \alpha}{\sqrt{M_\infty^2 - 1}}, \quad C_{D,\text{wave}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{M_\infty^2 - 1}} \left( \alpha^2 + \overline{\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2} \right)$$ 2. title: Foundations & Paradigms of Physics-Informed ML
content: 1. The Core Dilemma: Pure Data-Driven ML vs. First-Principles Physics Traditional machine learning algorithms excel at interpolating high-dimensional patterns within the convex hull of their training distribution. However, when applied to physical and industrial systems, standard neural networks suffer from four fundamental failure modes: Unphysical Extrapolation: Outside the training domain, pure black-box regressors violate elementary physical constraints (e.g., predicting negative mass, negative absolute temperatures, or non-zero divergence in incompressible flows). Prohibitive Sample Complexity: Training high-capacity deep networks from scratch requires $10^5 - 10^7$ labeled training samples. In mission-critical engineering, collecting real physical sensor telemetry is costly, slow, and constrained by sensor survivability limits. Severe Ill-Conditioning in Inverse Problems: Estimating hidden parameters (e.g., permeability fields, crack locations, thermal conductivity) from sparse boundary measurements is intrinsically ill-posed (Hadamard criterion); unconstrained models find spurious non-physical local minima. Spectral Bias: Standard multilayer perceptrons exhibit spectral bias toward low-frequency Fourier components, struggling to capture sharp physical shock fronts, boundary layers, and turbulent cascades without explicit inductive bias. Physics-Informed Machine Learning resolves this dilemma by integrating first-principles governing laws directly into neural architectures, loss functions, and optimization graphs. 2.
